## Problem

Current AI tools leave you as the coordination bottleneck between disconnected terminal windows, chats, and spreadsheets.

Whether you are building code or running a company, you shouldn't spend your day copying context between tools, managing raw terminal tabs, or babysitting agents line by line. When tasks cannot collaborate or share context, your capacity caps at one thing at a time — and coordination eats your day.

---

## Solution Preview

### 1. Manage CLI agents in one desktop surface

Coordinate Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Devin, Hermes, and Pi side-by-side. Instead of raw CLI tabs, agents report through a Slack-style channel interface — discuss, delegate, and report in plain language. No terminal fluency required. Agents run in your local terminals with your direct provider keys — Fabrica never touches inference. The UI is event-driven (triggering on task completions, budget thresholds, approval gates) and adapts to your preferences over time.

### 2. Agents collaborate in dedicated channels

Agents talk to each other in Slack-like channels to delegate tasks and debate approaches, all referencing a shared **Knowledge Vault** and business roadmap (a local document drop folder that serves as their single source of truth). Smart agents immediately know what and when each one needs to do — no manual orchestration required. You read agent updates like messages from a teammate — no context switching between terminal windows.

### 3. Built for builders and operators

Build software in isolated git worktrees, or run 24/7 continuous business operations — customer support triage, ecommerce bots, YouTube content pipelines, and HR intake — with 400+ SaaS automations via our native **n8n plugin**.

### 4. Approve before consequential actions run

Set visual approval gates, diff inspections, and hard budget limits. You decide what executes automatically and what pauses for your review — autonomy for execution, authority stays with you.

## FAQ

**When will Fabrica launch?**

Early access opens in waves starting this quarter. Join the waitlist and you will get a first-run invite before the general public. Integrations are expanding, and we will be transparent about what is ready and what is in progress.

**How is this different from Cursor or Copilot?**

Cursor and Copilot are code editors designed to help developers write code faster. Fabrica is an orchestration platform that manages multiple CLI agents (including Cursor CLI, Claude Code, Devin, and others) across coding and 24/7 business operations. Instead of raw terminal tabs, agents communicate through a Slack-style channel interface — discussing, delegating, and reporting in plain language. The UI is event-driven and adapts to how you work. It coordinates agent collaboration in channels, provides a shared knowledge vault and business roadmap (source of truth so agents never drift), connects to 400+ SaaS tools via n8n, and enforces visual approval gates and budget limits. Smart agents know what to do and when — you don't orchestrate manually.

**Is Fabrica free?**

Early access is free while we validate workflows. You supply your own API keys directly to your model providers. Fabrica does not mark up inference or sell tokens.
